findings.issue_text: `getForLogin()` does not include `BROKER_PUBLIC` in its search options, so an IdP that later becomes ineligible for login can remain cached and still be returned to direct callers.
Collecting cached login results into `HashSet` loses the delegate’s ordering, including realm-vs-org grouping for `ALL`, and returns arbitrary order; use `LinkedHashSet`.

goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getForLogin()` does not include `BROKER_PUBLIC` in its search options, so an IdP that later becomes ineligible for login can remain cached and still be returned to direct callers.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the diff, `getLoginPredicate()` in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java` is updated to include `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which does check BROKER_PUBLIC. Additionally, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate()` properly invalidates caches when an IDP's login eligibility changes. The cache invalidation logic in `registerIDPLoginInvalidation()` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate()` uses `getLoginPredicate()` to determine if caches need invalidation. When an IDP becomes ineligible for login, the update path will detect this change and invalidate the caches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collecting cached login results into `HashSet` loses the delegate’s ordering, including realm-vs-org grouping for `ALL`, and returns arbitrary order; use `LinkedHashSet`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in the `getForLogin` method, cached IDP IDs are collected into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` (line 'Set<IdentityProviderModel> identityProviders = new HashSet<>();'). HashSet does not preserve insertion order, so any ordering from the delegate (such as realm-vs-org grouping for FetchMode.ALL) would be lost. The finding correctly identifies that using LinkedHashSet would preserve the order. This is a real correctness issue if the ordering matters for the login page display.
